profile.onboarding: Icon-driven menus, with smart-steering and auto-accelerate assist options that let very young or new players just point and go.
profile.controls: Steer, accelerate, and use items; assists can reduce this to essentially one-stick play.
profile.core_loop: Race a short multi-lap course, using items and shortcuts to place as high as possible.
profile.goals_and_rewards: Race placement, trophies, and cosmetic/kart unlocks reward both winning and repeated play.
profile.difficulty_curve: Multiple speed (CC) classes plus AI rubber-banding keep races close regardless of skill level.
profile.game_feel: Considered best-in-class for kart racing, with highly tactile drift and boost feedback.
profile.art_and_audio: Bright, iconic characters with lively, upbeat music throughout races.
profile.session_length: About 2-3 minutes per race, roughly 10 minutes for a full cup of races.
profile.usability: Assist modes specifically let 4-6-year-olds complete races and feel successful.
profile.accessibility: Smart steering and auto-accelerate options remove the fine motor/timing demands of manual driving.
profile.ads_and_purchases: None on Nintendo Switch; the mobile Tour version has included gacha-style 'pipe' loot mechanics, which is a monetization pattern to avoid.
profile.notes: Worth checking whether Rolly Bally's Race mode needs an easier/assisted variant for the 5-7 bracket the way Mario Kart offers assists, given the profile flags time-pressure concerns for that age group.
